statement.text: A pro-p group is (relatively) strictly finitely presented if it is the pro-p completion of a group that is finitely presented (respectively, finitely presented in some finitely-based variety of groups). A pro-p group is finitely axiomatizable if it is determined up to isomorphism by a single sentence in the first-order language of group theory. (a) Does there exist a (relatively) strictly finitely presented pro-p group that is not finitely axiomatizable in the class of all pro-p groups? (b) In particular, is every finitely generated free pro-p group finitely axiomatizable?
